key_insight: Advanced home energy management delivers modest annual savings in electrified Belgian dwellings, potentially outweighed by purchase and subscription costs.
engineering_relevance: Controller selection involves trade-offs: MPC saves more money, while TreeC improves EV charge completion and smooths aggregate electricity demand.
method: Simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings with heat pumps, electric boilers, EV chargers, and photovoltaic adoption matching current rates.
Compare decision-tree-based TreeC and model predictive control (MPC) against default rule-based control.
Use perfect-forecast MPC as an upper bound under 2023 hourly electricity prices and a monthly peak tariff.
evidence_signal: Average annual savings versus rule-based control were €82.5 for TreeC, €116.6 for MPC, and €177.4 for perfect-forecast MPC, with similar thermal comfort across controllers.
watch_item: Simulation savings may not justify reported EMS purchase costs of €280–680 plus subscriptions of €0–360 per year.
paper_title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
